subproblem.title: Points with infinite fibre have Hⁿ-null projection, given Eilenberg's inequality (Dall'Alba Lemma 5.4)
subproblem.statement: Assume Eilenberg's inequality in the exact frozen form of the root-level node eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality: for all N, m, k ∈ ℕ there is C ≥ 0 such that for every A ⊆ ℝ^N, every L ≥ 0 and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^N → ℝ^m there is a measurable g : ℝ^m → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for all y and ∫ g dLᵐ ≤ C·Lᵐ·H^{m+k}(A). Then for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, every n-dimensional subspace W ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with orthogonal projection P := W.starProjection, and every A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with Hⁿ(A) < ∞: Hⁿ(P({a ∈ A : {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} is infinite})) = 0 (note {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} = A ∩ (a + W^⊥)).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (N m k : ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ (A : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ g : Rn m → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ y, μHE[k] (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) ≤ g y) ∧ ∫⁻ y, g y ≤ ((C * L ^ m : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[m + k] A) → ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))), finrank ℝ W = n → ∀ A : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), μHE[n] A < ∞ → μHE[n] (W.starProjection '' {a | a ∈ A ∧ {b | b ∈ A ∧ W.starProjection b = W.starProjection a}.Infinite}) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is Step 7 of the parent proof (M. G. Dall'Alba, The Besicovitch-Federer Projection Theorem, Lemma 5.4). The parent uses the root-level sibling eilenberg_inequality there; since a child of this decomposition can only depend on its own siblings, this child takes that sibling's exact frozen statement as the explicit hypothesis (Eil), which the parent discharges with the accepted declaration eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality.

Notation. N := n + ℓ, P := W.starProjection, π : ℝ^N → W the orthogonal projection viewed as a map into the subspace (so P = incl ∘ π), H⁰ := μHE[0], Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), and
 A₃ := {a ∈ A : {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} is infinite} (note {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa} = A ∩ (a + W^⊥)).

1. An isometric chart. Since finrank W = n, fix a linear isometric equivalence ι : ℝⁿ ≃ W and put f := ι⁻¹ ∘ π : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ and J := incl ∘ ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N. Since |π x − π x′| = |P(x − x′)| ≤ |x − x′| and ι⁻¹ is an isometry, f is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith 1 f). For all x, b, a ∈ ℝ^N: Px = J(f x), and f b = f a ⟺ π b = π a ⟺ Pb = Pa.

2. Applying (Eil). Apply (Eil) with (N, m, k) := (n + ℓ, n, 0): it gives C ≥ 0 such that, for the set A, the map f and L := 1, there is a measurable g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] with H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ and ∫ g dLⁿ ≤ C·1ⁿ·μHE[n + 0](A) = C·Hⁿ(A) < ∞.

3. g is finite almost everywhere. A measurable function with finite integral is finite a.e. (Mathlib ae_lt_top), so the measurable set {y : g(y) = ∞} is Lⁿ-null.

4. Infinite sets have infinite H⁰-measure. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Singletons are Borel, so H⁰(F) = #F for every finite F by finite additivity, and if S is infinite then H⁰(S) ≥ H⁰(F) = #F for finite subsets F ⊆ S of every cardinality; hence H⁰(S) = ∞.

5. For a ∈ A₃, by 1, A ∩ f⁻¹{f(a)} = {b ∈ A : Pb = Pa}, which is infinite; by 4 and 2, ∞ = H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{f(a)}) ≤ g(f(a)). Thus f(A₃) ⊆ {g = ∞}, and Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0 by 3 (monotonicity of the outer measure).

6. Transfer to W. By 1, P(A₃) = J(f(A₃)). J is an isometry, so Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Hⁿ(f(A₃)) (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Therefore Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0, i.e. μHE[n] (W.starProjection '' A₃) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write P = J ∘ f with f := ι⁻¹ ∘ (projection onto W) : ℝ^N → ℝⁿ 1-Lipschitz and J : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N a linear isometry onto W; fibres of f are the sets {Pb = Pa}.
Eilenberg (hypothesis, N := n+ℓ, m := n, k := 0, L := 1) gives a measurable g ≥ H⁰(A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) with ∫ g dLⁿ ≤ C·Hⁿ(A) < ∞, so g < ∞ Lⁿ-a.e.
H⁰ is counting measure, so infinite fibres force g(f(a)) = ∞: f(A₃) lies in an Lⁿ-null set.
Isometry invariance of Hⁿ and μHE[n] = volume on ℝⁿ give Hⁿ(P(A₃)) = Lⁿ(f(A₃)) = 0.

audit.reason: The explicit Eilenberg hypothesis matches the existing dependency's frozen type exactly. Applying it with m=n, k=0 and L=1 gives a finite-integral majorant. Infinite fibres have infinite H⁰ measure, so their images lie in its null infinite-value set; isometry invariance transfers nullity to W.
